_comment: Minimal realm for the node's integration tests. A fixture, not a copy of the
production realm — see CONTRACT.md for what it is guaranteeing and why the node does
Applied through the Admin API by tests/harness/keycloak.py, not by Keycloak's realm
import. Import treats every list-shaped collection as a whole-realm snapshot: declaring
one client scope removes the fourteen built-in ones, and declaring one role strips
account access from default-roles. Applying object by object avoids all of that.

audienceScopes.// circuless-cloud: The Cloud API's audience. A node client gets it as a DEFAULT scope, because talking to the Cloud API is the only thing a node token is for (N17).
audienceScopes.name: circuless-cloud

audienceScopes.// node:other-node: So a token for a DIFFERENT node can be minted, which N2 must reject.
audienceScopes.name: node:other-node

clients.// role: The browser client. Auth Code + PKCE, because H2 disables the password grant everywhere and the harness drives the real login flow.
A service principal of /orgs/alpha. private_key_jwt, unaffected by H2.

A node principal. Exists so the suite can present the token N2 must refuse with node_principal_not_permitted (D14). Given node audiences on purpose — the production realm withholds them, and the node must refuse the token on principal_type regardless.
clients.// scopes: circuless-cloud is OPTIONAL, not default. As a default it would ride along on every node token, so a node token that also named a node audience would carry two - and be refused on audience (401) before D14 could refuse it on principal type (403). One audience per token applies to nodes too.

clients.// role: A second node client, for N17. Enrollment replaces the registered certificate, so it must not happen on test-node-principal: that one is shared by every test that needs a node token, and swapping its certificate breaks them all. Found the hard way.

users.// consultant: Member of both organisations, for acting-org resolution (R11).

users.// admins.only: In /orgs/beta/admins but NOT /orgs/beta. An admin of an organisation is a member of it, whatever the operator remembered to click.

users.// odd.groups: Groups outside /orgs, and one nested deeper than an org. All must be ignored (G14).

users.// stranger: No organisation at all — a self-registered user nobody has admitted yet.

users.// no.principal.type: principal_type deliberately unset. The node must fail closed on this, not assume 'user' (CONTRACT.md property 5).
